final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrowing is meaningful but not sufficient to reach compliant_with_caveats here, because the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved compliance predicate under the stated policy. On the available evidence, the record may support a constrained launch-readiness judgment, but it does not adequately support the audited claim that certification without a material weakness disclosure is compliant. The key gap remains the same: a named committed segment misses target, legal review is still open, and there is no approved risk acceptance in evidence. Business-cost arguments and polished caveating do not cure that evidentiary deficiency.
remaining_concerns: The multilingual customer support segment still misses target by 1.1 percentage points.
That segment is named in two regional support commitments, which fits the stated materiality trigger.
The policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when named commitments are affected or legal review is pending.
Legal review on disclosure remains open, so a policy predicate for clean compliance is unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering this gap.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public monitoring/documentation guidance do not substitute for the internal disclosure requirement.
